label: Show reference overlay
summary: Shows or hides the map editor's reference overlay, a reference picture laid over the map.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Toggle reference texture overlay." button, passing the opposite of GetReferenceOverlayVisibility, so a click toggles it.

label: Toggle terrain color map
summary: Shows or hides the terrain color map overlay in the map editor.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Toggle terrain Color Map overlay."

label: Open log viewer
summary: Gives access to the central log viewer of the map editor.
details: The game's description says only "Access Central Log Viewer". Its own files never use it.

label: This map editor window
summary: Gives the map editor window itself, so a GUI element can hand it on.
details: Going by its name and by the same name in other windows, where a window is passed on as a whole. The game documents nothing more.

label: Overlay opacity
summary: How opaque (how little see-through) the map editor's reference overlay is, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla shows it on the "Overlay Opacity" slider and in the number box beside it, shown while the overlay is visible.

label: This map editor window
summary: The map editor window itself.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use `Self` in game texts, where it hands on the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set overlay opacity
summary: Sets how opaque the map editor's reference overlay is.
details: Vanilla calls it when the "Overlay Opacity" slider moves or typing in the number box is finished; the slider or box hands over the new value.

label: Open settings
summary: Opens the map editor's settings window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Open settings".

label: Toggle border options
summary: Shows or hides the map editor's border options.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Toggle borders options."

label: Toggle history
summary: Shows or hides the map editor's history window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the history button of the map editor's history toolbar. The GUI animation editors have the same call commented out, with a TODO note about hooking up their own history window.

label: Toggle overlay options
summary: Shows or hides the options of the map editor's reference overlay.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Toggle reference texture options."

label: This border layer
summary: The border layer itself, to hand it to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to MapEditorLayerBorderDockable.GetLayerName to show the layer's name in the "Force Showing Borders" list.

label: Layer index
summary: The number (position) of this border layer in the map editor, as a whole number.
details: Going by its name. The game's own files never use it.

label: Borders always shown
summary: Whether the borders of this layer are always shown in the map editor.
details: Vanilla uses it as the state of the layer's box in the "Force Showing Borders" list. Its tooltip says that otherwise the borders show only when the current tool needs them.

label: This border layer
summary: The border layer of the map editor itself.
details: Going by its name and by how `Self` is used on other types in game texts. The game documents nothing more.

label: Always show borders
summary: Sets whether the borders of this layer are always shown in the map editor.
details: Vanilla calls it from the layer's box in the "Force Showing Borders" list, passing the opposite of IsForceShown, so a click toggles it. When off, the borders show only when the current tool needs them.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether the borders are always shown.

label: This dockable border layer
summary: Gives the dockable border layer panel of the map editor itself, so a GUI element can hand it on.

label: Border layer name
summary: The name of the given border layer.
details: Vanilla shows it beside each layer's box in the map editor's "Force Showing Borders" list.

label: This dockable border layer
summary: The dockable border layer panel of the map editor itself.
details: Going by its name and by how `Self` is used on other types in game texts. The game documents nothing more.

label: This map mode
summary: Gives the map mode itself, so a GUI element can hand it on.
details: Going by its name and by the same name in other windows. The game documents nothing more.

label: Map mode icon
summary: The icon of a map mode.
details: Vanilla uses it as the picture (`texture`) of map mode buttons. Its return type is not registered, so the game does not name it.

label: Map mode key
summary: The internal key (name) of a map mode, as text.

label: Map mode name
summary: The display name of a map mode, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the label text of map mode entries (gui/shared/mapmodes.gui).

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the map mode has an icon.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla does not use it on map modes; other types have a function of the same name used for visibility, which is only a hint.

label: This map mode
summary: The map mode itself.
details: Going by its name and by how `Self` is used on other types in game texts. The game documents nothing more.

label: This mask
summary: Gives the map object mask itself, so a GUI element can hand it on.
details: Going by its name and by the same name in other windows. The game documents nothing more.

label: Generator names
summary: The names of the generators shown for this mask, as one text.

label: Mask preview

label: Is modified
summary: Whether this mask has been changed.

label: Is selected

label: This mask
summary: The map object mask itself.
details: Going by its name and by how `Self` is used on other types in game texts. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set modified
summary: Marks the mask as changed; it returns nothing.
details: Going by its name. The game's own files never use it.

label: Rename mask
summary: Gives this mask a new name.
details: Vanilla calls it when typing in the mask's name box is finished; the box hands over the new name, checked by GetTextValidator.

label: Select mask
summary: Makes this mask the one selected in the map object painter.
details: Vanilla calls it when the mask's row is clicked.

label: This painter
summary: Gives the map object painter itself, so a GUI element can hand it on.
details: Going by its name and by the same name in other windows. The game documents nothing more.

label: Text validator
summary: A validator for text typed into the map object painter's inputs.
details: Going by its name. The game does not register its return type, and its own files never use it.

label: Mark all masks modified
summary: Marks every mask of the map object painter as changed.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Mark all masks modified" button; its tooltip says this makes the generators run again on save.

label: Mask
summary: The list of masks of the map object painter.
details: Vanilla fills the painter's mask list from it, one row per mask with its preview, name and generator count.

label: This painter
summary: The map object painter itself.
details: Going by its name and by how `Self` is used on other types in game texts. The game documents nothing more.

label: This painter mode
summary: Gives the painter mode itself, so a GUI element can hand it on.
details: Going by its name and by the same name in other windows. The game documents nothing more.

label: Map object painter active
summary: Whether the map object painter is the tool chosen in the map editor.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the toolbox button with the tooltip "Map Object Painter".

label: This painter mode
summary: The painter mode itself.
details: Going by its name and by how `Self` is used on other types in game texts. The game documents nothing more.

label: Blur threshold setting
summary: The blur threshold setting of the map object painter, for its slider.
details: Vanilla hands it to the blur threshold slider, shown only while the painter's blend mode is Blur (which blurs the selected mask within the brush).

label: These painter options
summary: Gives the painter options themselves, so a GUI element can hand them on.
details: Going by its name and by the same name in other windows. The game documents nothing more.

label: Paint value
summary: The value the map object painter paints with, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla shows it on the "Value" slider and in the number box beside it, shown while the blend mode is Set.

label: Is blend mode
summary: Whether the given blend mode is the one the map object painter uses now.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the blend mode buttons and to show the options of the Set and Blur modes. The modes: Add (additive), Sub (subtractive), Set, and Blur (blurs the selected mask within the brush).

label: These painter options
summary: The painter options themselves.
details: Going by its name and by how `Self` is used on other types in game texts. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set blend mode
summary: Chooses how the map object painter combines what it paints with the mask.
details: Vanilla calls it from the blend mode buttons: additive, subtractive, set, and blur (blurs the selected mask within the brush).

label: Set paint value
summary: Sets the value the map object painter paints with.
details: Vanilla calls it when the "Value" slider moves; the slider hands over the new value. SetPaintValueStr does the same from the number box.

label: Set paint value from text
summary: Sets the value the map object painter paints with from typed text.
details: Vanilla calls it when typing in the number box beside the "Value" slider is finished; the box hands over its text.

label: This tool
summary: Gives the map object tool itself, so a GUI element can hand it on.
details: Going by its name and by the same name in other windows. The game documents nothing more.

label: Map object tooltip
summary: The tooltip shown over the map by the map editor's map object tool.
details: It gives a GuiEditorTooltip object; vanilla's map editor tooltip shows its title and description when it has them.

label: Is spawning mode
summary: Whether the map object tool is in its mode for placing new objects.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the button with the tooltip "Spawning global objects mode."

label: Is move mode
summary: Whether the map object tool is set to move the selected objects.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the button with the tooltip "Move selected objects around."

label: Is rotate mode
summary: Whether the map object tool is set to rotate the selected objects.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the button with the tooltip "Rotate selected objects."

label: Is scale mode
summary: Whether the map object tool is set to resize the selected objects.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the button with the tooltip "Scale selected objects."

label: Is territory selection
summary: Whether the map object tool selects territories instead of single objects.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the button with the tooltip "Territory selection mode."

label: Is object selection
summary: Whether the map object tool selects single map objects.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the button with the tooltip "Objects selection mode."

label: Move tool
summary: The move tool of the map object editor.
details: Its kind is Promote, so it leads on to another object (a MoveTool). Going by its name. The game's own files never use it.

label: Rotate randomly
summary: Turns the selected map objects to random directions.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Randomly rotate selected map objects."

label: Select tool
summary: The select tool of the map editor's map object tool.
details: Vanilla goes on from it to IsHideSelection and SetHideSelection, for the button with the tooltip "Hide the selection graphics".

label: This tool
summary: The map object tool itself.
details: Going by its name and by how `Self` is used on other types in game texts. The game documents nothing more.

label: Use spawning mode
summary: Switches the map object tool to its mode for placing new objects.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Spawning global objects mode."

label: Use move mode
summary: Switches the map object tool to moving the selected objects.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Move selected objects around."

label: Use rotate mode
summary: Switches the map object tool to rotating the selected objects.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Rotate selected objects."

label: Use scale mode
summary: Switches the map object tool to resizing the selected objects.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Scale selected objects."

label: Territory selection mode
summary: Switches the map objects tool of the engine's map editor to selecting territories; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the toolbar button with the tooltip 'Territory selection mode.'; the button shows its state through a separate function. The other mode selects single objects.

label: Object selection mode
summary: Switches the map objects tool of the engine's map editor to selecting map objects; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the toolbar button with the tooltip 'Objects selection mode.'; the other mode selects territories instead.

label: This marriage info
summary: Gives the marriage info object itself, so a GUI element can hand it on.
details: Going by its name and by the same name in other windows. The game documents nothing more.

label: Alliance items
summary: The list of alliance entries of the marriage info.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source (`datamodel`) of a list in the marriage interaction templates (gui/interaction_templates.gui). Going by its name, the entries are alliances; the game does not say more.

label: Base marriage offer
summary: The base offer of the marriage info.
details: Vanilla hands it on as the data of parts of the marriage window and the marriage notification window. Going by its name, it is the offer before any extras. Its return type is not registered.

label: Grand wedding promise text
summary: The description text of the grand wedding promise.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the marriage window (gui/interaction_marriage.gui).

label: House relation change
summary: The number by which the marriage changes the relation between two houses.
details: Vanilla uses it in the text that tells how the relation between the second actor's house and the second recipient's house will change (MARRIAGE_IMPACT_ON_HOUSE_RELATION).

label: Marriage icon frame
summary: Which frame (number) of the marriage icon picture to show.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `frame` of an icon in the marriage notification window and the interaction templates. Going by its name, it picks the icon that fits the kind of marriage.

label: Marriage or betrothal
summary: The word that says whether this is a marriage or a betrothal, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the whole text of MARRIAGE_INFO. Going by its name, it gives "marriage" or "betrothal" depending on the case.

label: Matrilineal text
summary: The description text about a matrilineal marriage, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text line in the interaction templates (gui/interaction_templates.gui), only when the match is not same-sex. Another text next to it is shown only while this text is empty (and the match is not same-sex).

label: New house relation level
summary: The level the relation between two houses will have after the marriage.
details: Vanilla uses it in the text MARRIAGE_IMPACT_ON_HOUSE_RELATION that describes the change between two houses. Its return type is not registered, so the game does not name it.

label: Secondary actor's house
summary: The house of the secondary actor of the marriage.
details: Vanilla chains it with a house's name in MARRIAGE_IMPACT_ON_HOUSE_RELATION, which is the first of the two houses named there. The secondary actor is the second person on the actor's side, not the main one.

label: Secondary recipient's house
summary: The house of the secondary recipient of the marriage.
details: Vanilla chains it with a house's name in MARRIAGE_IMPACT_ON_HOUSE_RELATION, which is the second of the two houses named there. The secondary recipient is the second person on the recipient's side.

label: Has alliances
summary: Whether the marriage comes with alliances.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its opposite, to show or hide parts of the interaction templates.

label: Has house relation change
summary: Whether the marriage changes the relation between houses.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the house relation part of the interaction templates.

label: Is grand wedding promised
summary: Whether a grand wedding is promised with this marriage.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of a checkbox in the marriage window.

label: Can promise grand wedding
summary: Whether the grand wedding promise can be chosen.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of the grand wedding checkbox in the marriage window. Going by that, it says whether the choice is allowed.

label: Is matrilineal
summary: Whether the marriage is matrilineal.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of a checkbox in the marriage window.

label: This marriage info
summary: The marriage info object itself.
details: Going by its name and by how `Self` is used on other types in game texts. The game documents nothing more.

label: Toggle grand wedding promise
summary: Switches the grand wedding promise on or off; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it when the grand wedding checkbox in the marriage window is clicked.

label: Toggle matrilineal

details: Vanilla runs it when the matrilineal checkbox in the marriage window is clicked.

label: Can clear marry-off
summary: Whether the marry-off choice can be cleared.

details: Going by its name and by the same name in other windows. The game documents nothing more.

summary: The marriage offer itself.

summary: The mask entry itself.

summary: Gives the mask painter manager itself, so a GUI element can hand it on.
details: Going by its name and by the same name in other windows. The game documents nothing more.

summary: Empties the search filter of the mask painter's mask list; it returns nothing.

summary: The search filter text of the mask painter's mask list.
details: Vanilla shows it in the filter box above the list. The box's tooltip says several search keys can be separated with the | sign.

summary: The notes text of the selected mask in the mask painter.
details: Vanilla shows it in the multi-line Notes box of the mask settings, which appear only while a mask is selected.

details: Vanilla enables the Clone and Delete buttons only then, and shows the mask settings (mask type and notes) only then.

summary: Whether the selected mask is a developer mask.

summary: Clears the selected mask in the mask painter; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the button with the tooltip 'Clear the selected mask.', which is enabled only when the mask can be changed.

summary: Makes a copy of the selected mask in the mask painter; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the button with the tooltip 'Clone selected mask.', which is enabled only while a mask is selected.

label: Delete mask
summary: Deletes the selected mask in the mask painter; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the button with the tooltip 'Delete selected mask.', which is enabled only while a mask is selected.

label: New mask

details: Vanilla runs it from the button with the tooltip 'Add new mask.', the first of the mask actions.

label: Rename mask

details: Vanilla runs it from the button with the tooltip 'Rename selected mask.', which is enabled only when the mask can be changed. How the new name is entered is not shown.

label: Set mask notes

label: Toggle local mask

details: Vanilla runs it from the Local Mask check box. Local masks are saved only on this computer and are not pushed to the repository.

label: This mask painter viewport
summary: Gives the mask painter viewport itself, so a GUI element can hand it on.
details: Going by its name and by the same name in other windows. The game documents nothing more.

label: Map view tooltip
summary: The tooltip of the mask painter's map view, as an editor tooltip object.
details: Its kind is Promote: it leads on to a GuiEditorTooltip, whose own functions fill the tooltip. Vanilla sets it as the data of the map editor's viewport tooltip in the mask painter's map view.
